findings.evidence: Statement at line 62: `theorem galEquivZMod_arithFrobAt [IsGalois ℚ K] [Finite (𝓞 K ⧸ Q)] (hp : p.Coprime n)` — no `Odd n` or `p ≠ 2` hypothesis anywhere; the PR description itself says "Both equations include `p = 2` without an oddness assumption."
findings.fix: Delete the sentence, or state the actual content: no oddness hypothesis is imposed; `hp` already covers `p = 2`.
findings.issue: "The formula holds also at `p = 2` when `n` is odd." presents an oddness side condition that does not exist: the only hypothesis is `hp : p.Coprime n`, which for `p = 2` is exactly `n` odd. Worse, the sentence sits only on `galEquivZMod_arithFrobAt`, suggesting the general `galEquivZMod_eq_unitOfCoprime_of_isArithFrobAt` is more restricted — it is not.

findings.evidence: `galEquivZMod_eq_two_of_isArithFrobAt_two` (line 38) has the same shape and hypotheses as the odd-prime statements at lines 46, 54, 63, 71; nothing distinguishes `p = 2`.
findings.fix: Drop it, or say the concrete thing — the exponent is `p mod 5`, not `p⁻¹ mod 5` (arithmetic, not geometric Frobenius) — uniformly for all five primes.
findings.issue: Same problem class: "In particular, the dyadic case uses the same arithmetic normalization as the odd primes." No case in the file is normalized differently, and "arithmetic normalization" is left undefined, so the remark is vacuous as written.
The cross-reference `Cyclotomic.FiveSplitting` is not a resolvable module name or namespace, so a reader cannot locate the complementary results.

findings.evidence: `Cyclotomic/Frobenius.lean:41` keeps proof-level commentary under `## Implementation notes`; the new file puts it in the opening description.
findings.fix: Remove it, or move it under an `## Implementation notes` heading as the existing `Cyclotomic/Frobenius.lean` does for proof-level discussion.
findings.issue: "The proof uses `TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_iff_galEquivZMod_eq_absNorm` and the comparison between the base rings `𝓞 ℚ` and `ℤ` in `Ideal.IntegersRat`." — module docstring describing the proof route rather than the material; it goes stale the moment the proof is rewritten.

summary: Both files have module docstrings and every public theorem is documented, but two docstrings carry a spurious "dyadic case" caveat that states a condition already implied by the hypothesis, one module docstring narrates the proof route, and a cross-reference uses a non-resolvable module path.
